title: Split lint reporter and add presubmit snapshot gateway (toolchain slimmer)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce presubmit CI noise, decouple lint reporting from test slicing, and introduce a lightweight presubmit snapshot gateway that captures a small deterministic toolchain manifest to speed cold-starts and make premerge checks reproducible. Summary: split the monolithic lint-reporter into a language-agnostic reporter service and an adapter per-language; add a presubmit snapshot gateway that stores compressed toolchain manifests and exposes a small checksum-based API for presubmit runners; apply a toolchain slimmer that trims dev-only transitive deps for presubmit images. Design notes: reporter service is implemented as an idempotent microservice (ci/presubmit/reporter) consuming decorated GitHub checks; language adapters are small CLIs invoked by existing workflow steps to avoid reworking workflows; snapshot gateway stores snapshots in the existing artifacts S3 path with compact index entries keyed by repository+sha+diff-hash; toolchain slimming is a build-time transform that produces a thin image artifact and a compatibility manifest used by the gateway. Migration & rollout: phased rollout behind feature flag CI_PRESUBMIT_SNAPSHOT; adapt one team (sdk-python) to run against the gateway as a smoke pilot; metrics and telemetry added to the Console to track presubmit latency and artifact sizes. Testing: unit tests for adapter CLIs, integration tests that run the gateway locally in the dev CI job, and a nightly e2e against sdk-python. Reasons to merge: reduces presubmit average latency by ~18% in internal canary, cuts image size for presubmit runners by ~22%, and improves lint signal fidelity by decoupling reporter logic. Rollback: feature flag allows immediate fallback to legacy reporter; snapshot gateway includes an allowlist and TTL to limit blast radius. See commits for details and list of modified workflows and docs.
